subject.title: feat(gateway): wire read coding tool into HTTP /tools/invoke (narrow)

question: Should OpenClaw permanently support owner-gated built-in host-filesystem `read` over Gateway direct invoke behind `gateway.tools.directInvoke.hostFsRead` plus the existing allowlist?
rationale: The capability is absent from current `main` and creates a deliberate sensitive-data API plus a permanent public configuration surface; code review can validate safeguards but cannot choose that product security boundary.

options.title: Accept read-only direct invoke
options.body: Approve after the documentation defects are fixed and exact-head proof confirms owner-only built-in reads, default denial, plugin compatibility, and audit visibility.

options.title: Require plugin-owned reads
options.body: Keep built-in filesystem tools out of Gateway direct invoke and rely on plugins or external automation for deterministic reads.

options.title: Design one coding-tool policy first
options.body: Pause this PR and the write/edit extension until maintainers define one canonical direct-invoke security contract for coding tools.

recommendation.title: Accept read-only direct invoke
recommendation.body: Approve after the documentation defects are fixed and exact-head proof confirms owner-only built-in reads, default denial, plugin compatibility, and audit visibility.

likelyOwner.reason: BunsDev hardened and merged the shared `tools.invoke` contract that this new security boundary extends.
